newsitem.title: USA: NHL-CANADIENS RALLY TO TIE PENGUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-CANADIENS RALLY TO TIE PENGUINS.

text.p: Stephane Richer batted a shot past Ken Wregget with just under two minutes to go in regulation as the Montreal Canadiens used a third-period rally to tie the Pittsburgh Penguins, 2-2 on Monday.
Montreal coach Mario Tremblay pulled goaltender Jocelyn Thibault for an extra attacker with 2:29 remaining and Richer made the gamble pay off.
Valeri Bure also scored in the third period for the Canadiens.
"If there's one thing I'm proud of my players tonight it would be that they never quit," Canadiens coach Mario Tremblay said. "They never, ever quit."
In Toronto, Darby Hendrickson scored with an extra attacker with 42 seconds left in regulation, lifting the Toronto Maple Leafs into a 3-3 tie with the Dallas Stars.
Trailing 3-2, the Leafs pulled goaltender Felix Potvin for a sixth skater with 80 seconds left.

Steve Sullivan had the puck in the right corner along the boards and fed a pass behind the net. Mats Sundin slid it in front to Hendrickson, who beat Arturs Irbe between the pads for his 10th goal of the season.
Todd Warriner had two goals for Toronto.
In Chicago, Jim Cummins scored the tying goal early in the second period and Jeff Hackett made 35 saves as the Chicago Blackhawks salvaged a 2-2 tie with the Vancouver Canucks.
Cummins and Murray Craven had goals for Chicago, ending long scoring droughts. The Blackhawks are 0-1-2 in their last three games and have just one win (1-3-3) in their last seven.
Lonny Bohonos and Markus Naslund scored power-play goals in a 2:27 span of the first period for Vancouver.

In Phoenix, Ron Tugnutt made 21 saves and Alexei Yashin, Steve Duchesne and Daniel Alfredsson each had a goal and an assist as the Ottawa Senators ended a four-game losing streak with a 4-1 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes.

Alexandre Daigle also tallied for Ottawa, which won for just the second time in nine games (2-6-1). The Senators vaulted over the New York Islanders into 11th place in the Eastern Conference, four points out of the final playoff spot.

"We wanted to get ahead and play with the lead," Ottawa coach Jacques Martin said. "You play a club that has three shutouts in a row, plus a team that hasn't played well at home, we wanted to make sure we scored first and come out hard and that was the difference."
Jim Johnson had the lone goal for Phoenix.

In Los Angeles, Ray Ferraro's breakaway goal with 7:38 left in regulation capped a three-goal comeback as the Los Angeles Kings rallied for a 3-3 tie against the Detroit Red Wings, who are unbeaten in 11 straight games.
Detroit scored twice in the first period and once in the second, but Sean O'Donnell's fifth goal of the season with 8:45 remaining in the second period began the comeback.
Ed Olczyk scored his 21st with 50 seconds to go in the second period, drawing the Kings within one, and Ferraro's 23rd goal tied it.
